newsitem.title: USA: Floundering outright crudes fail to move US grades.
newsitem.headline: Floundering outright crudes fail to move US grades.

text.p: Domestic grade barrels in the U.S. Gulf held onto steady differentials against a slumping outright crude market Thursday afternoon.

September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was some 40 cents weaker at $19.85-95 a barrel, actually trimming losses from earlier when lows came on the NYMEX market at $19.65 a barrel. September/October spreads remained at minus 7-9 cents.
Gasoline selling in the expiring August NYMEX contract was blamed for the crude price retreat.

Grade busines saw Midland/WTI and Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James barrels sell at stagnant prices, with Midland moving at 29 cents under WTI and LLS at premiums of 23 and 24 cents to the September WTI/Cushing.
Other trades had Postings Plus selling at $1.95 and West Texas Sour/Midland at $1.40 and $1.38 under September WTI.

Market news featured a couple of supply disruptions, notably reports of a fire at the 310,000 barrels per day (bpd) Curacao refinery operated by Petroleos de Venezuala in the Caribbean. Production was cut after a fire downed one distillation unit Thursday morning, trimming production from 180,000 bpd to 60,000 bpd.
Earlier, Cano Limon field operator Occidental Petroleum Corp said Colombian rebels blasted the country's main pipeline Wednesday night, the 43rd such attack in 1997.
Pipeline runs were halted, and repairs slated for completion by Friday night. Cano field production and exports were not impacted, Occidental said.

Also, the return of Iraq to world oil export markets looked increasingly likely for the first part to middle of August. U.N. officials said only minor points remained to be solved before Secretary-General Kofi Annan aprroves the aid distribution plan necessary for implementing second round "oil-for-food" accord sales.
